title: Kevin Sells: Setalcott Family Historian
summary: A Setalcott descendant and family historian who connects relatives’ memories with Setauket’s museums and community gatherings.
content:
Kevin Sells is identified in published reporting as a Setalcott descendant, historian and archivist. His work illustrates how family knowledge contributes to the history of a place, including when descendants live away from their ancestral community.1

Remembering people behind the exhibits

In July 2023, historian Beverly C. Tyler interviewed Sells during a return visit to Setauket. They visited the Chicken Hill exhibition at the Three Village Historical Society and restored rubber-factory worker houses. Sells shared memories of Sarah Ann Sells, a family matriarch and midwife, and family reunions that kept relatives connected. Tyler presents these as Sells’s recollections, bringing lived experience into the museum’s account.2

History carried through relationships

His cousin Helen Sells helped arrange that meeting during his visit for the Setalcott Corn Festival Powwow. The interview shows family history being passed between relatives, a community gathering and a local historian.2

Continue with Setauket Ancestral Land. Mapped connections are public-history places, not private family homes or a reconstructed journey.

References
  1. Leanne Pastore, “Rediscovering Setauket’s Indigenous legacy,” The Stony Brook Press, October 22, 2025. Unpaginated; identification of Kevin Sells as a Setalcott descendant and historian/archivist.
  2. Beverly C. Tyler, “Former Setauket resident renews his connection to area,” The Village Times Herald, July 20, 2023, p. A4 (PDF page 4). Interview with Kevin Sells; museum visit and family memories.
why_this_matters: Family historians help restore names, relationships and everyday experiences to places that might otherwise be remembered only through buildings and official records.
